Resolves #18675

🌿 A guide documented an engine-reserved sigil by writing it down, and the page answered by printing the whole document again underneath — after this, a code span the reader authored can no longer address the text around it.

**What this delivers.** `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` authors two mermaid fences and the portal showed four diagrams, each one twice, about seven thousand pixels apart. The cause is one character pair in a string replacement, and it was never about mermaid.

**The mechanism.** Ticket protection swaps every fenced and inline code span for a token, runs the ticket-id replacement, then restores each token with `content.replace(token, value)` — where `value` is the restored code **as a string**. A string replacement gives `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$n` special meaning. That guide documents an engine-reserved sigil by authoring the inline code `` `$` ``, which restores as `$` followed by a backtick: JS reads that as *insert everything before the match* and splices the entire preceding document back into the page. The fences at lines 42 and 95 sit before it, so the duplicate carries both as raw markdown and `processMermaidBlocks` — which runs later — mints four ids for two authored fences.

It also explains the shape that made this hard to read. The spliced copy lands mid-line, so its `#` is no longer at line start and never becomes a second `<h1>`; marked renders it inside the surrounding list item. A probe that counts `h1` elements therefore reports exactly one and concludes the body is not duplicated. The ticket's own Avoided Traps table records that reading, and it is what sent the first investigation looking for a re-render.

**Both restore loops take a function replacement**, which is returned verbatim. The second one carries highlighted HTML — arbitrary text with the same exposure, and the same defect waiting for the first code block containing `$&`.

Evidence: L3 (live portal rendering on this host — `value` versus published `html` per guide, plus the ticket's own e2e witness) → L3 required (the ACs are about what a reader sees; the unit arm is L2 and runs in CI). No residual claimed: every AC is met at this head.

| AC-2 | `test/playwright/e2e/portal/LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` — **3 passed** at this head, the control arm and its live-preview sibling together |
| AC-3 | Named above with the measurement that established it: `DockLayouts.md:222` is the file's only `` $` `` sequence, `src/app/content/Component.mjs:48` sets `replaceTicketIds: true`, and the restore at `Markdown.mjs:340` was the string replacement. The doubling is present in `html` and absent from `value`, and four *distinct* placeholder ids place it before `processMermaidBlocks` |
| AC-4 | Red-first, and for the duplication specifically rather than a bare count: the new unit arm asserts a sentinel sentence survives exactly once through `modifyMarkdown`. Clean tree **1 failed / 41 passed**; this head **42 passed** |
| AC-5 | The three single-fence guides still render one diagram each — `DockLayoutsWindows` 1, `DockLayoutsStyling` 1, `DockLayoutsFirstLayout` 1 — so nothing passes by suppressing rendering |

## Deltas from ticket

**The blast radius was three guides, not one.** `DockLayoutsAdoption` (1 fence → 2 placeholders) and `DockLayoutsPanes` (1 fence → 2) carry the same sequence and were doubling the same way; both render correctly after the repair. The ticket scoped this to one guide because the census happened to sample only guides that do not contain `` $` `` — `grep -rlF '$\`' learn/` returns exactly these three.

The second restore loop in `processReadonlyCodeBlocks` is repaired alongside the first. It has no reproducer in the corpus today, so it is a latent sibling rather than a fix — but leaving one of two identical unsafe restores repaired would be the worse outcome.

## Evolution

Three readings were wrong before this one, and each was corrected by a measurement rather than by argument. First I inferred from a doubled *title* that the body was duplicated; the ancestor chains showed the second occurrence was an auto-generated contents list, so I withdrew it and re-measured with mid-body prose, which a contents list cannot carry — that held. Then the instrumented run counted one fetch, one value set and one render and produced **one** placeholder where an unpatched run produced four, which looked like proof the route mattered; running both navigation paths unpatched gave identical results, so the real finding was that patching suppresses the defect and a patch-based probe cannot measure it. That is what forced reading the component's own configs instead, which is the measurement that localised the doubling to between `value` and `html` and made the rest arithmetic.
